newsitem.title: ITALY: Berlusconi committal hearing adjourned to Dec 18.
newsitem.headline: Berlusconi committal hearing adjourned to Dec 18.

text.p: A committal hearing to decide if Italian media tycoon Silvio Berlusconi should stand trial for allegedly setting up an illegal slush fund when his Fininvest group bought a film company in 1988 was adjourned on Wednesday until December 18.
The preliminary hearing, before examining magistrate Cristina Mannocci, opened on Tuesday.

Berlusconi, who served as prime minister for seven months in 1994 and leads Italy's centre-right Freedom Alliance, and four others are accused by Milan state prosecutor Margherita Taddei of falsifying company accounts and embezzling funds.

Taddei accuses the five men of paying more for the purchase of film company Medusa than the 28 billion lire ($18 million) written down in Fininvest's balance sheet. The extra amount was said to have been used to establish a slush fund.
The other four men, all close business associates of Berlusconi, are Adriano Galliani, Giancarlo Foscale, Carlo Bernasconi and Livio Gironi.

Berlusconi, already on trial in Milan on charges of bribing tax inspectors in return for lenient audits of his companies, faces a new court hearing later this month, accused of illegally channelling funds to politicians.
